question.text: A pivotal battle during the Pacific Theatre was this one, taking place in an atoll at the end of the Hawaiian island chain, in which American forces sank four Japanese carriers. An airport in Chicago is named for it.
question.clue: Admiral Nagumo's indecisiveness about bombing the island or carriers left his fleet vulnerable in this battle.

swap.leadin: In 1845, a British flagstaff was controversially cut down in this modern country, sparking a year of war.
swap.text: Name this Oceanic nation consisting of a North Island, South Island, and many small islands roughly one thousand miles east of Australia.
swap.clue: This country's nuclear-free policy was enacted by David Lange, who was prime minister when a Greenpeace ship protesting nuclear tests in Polynesia was bombed in this country.

question.text: The silver fern is also a common motif in the art of these indigenous New Zealanders. These peoples signed the Treaty of Waitangi for peace with the British, and are often compared to Australian Aborigines.
question.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

swap.text: Tourists often laugh when they discover that even Hawaii has "interstate highways," something that manylearn upon landing at Daniel Inouye[ee-noh-ay]InternationalAirport in this city.
swap.clue: This capital city of Hawaii. It is home to the only royal palace in the USA, Iolani Palace, as well as Waikiki Beach.

question.text: Frank Bainimarama has ruled this South Pacific country since a 2006 coup. Tension between the native Melanesians and those of Indian descent makes up a significant part of this country's politics.
question.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

swap.text: This island chain is the last British holding in the Pacific Ocean. It is mainly inhabited by descendants of mutineers from the HMS Bounty.
swap.clue: Police officer Gail Cox denounced the culture of sexual abuse on this island, the subject of a controversial 2004 trial that convicted six of its residents.

question.leadin: The successful voyage of this vessel supported the idea that contact between South America and Polynesia happened before the Europeans came.
question.text: Name the balsa wood raft that crossed the Pacific in 1947.

swap.text: Lili'uokalani was the last sovereign ruler of this kingdom until it was annexed by the United States in 1898.
swap.clue: Its final ruler was forced to sign Lorrin Thurston's Bayonet Constitution, and this kingdom was succeeded by a republic led by Sanford Dole.

question.leadin: The second ruler of this name abolished the tapu code of conduct.
question.text: Give this name of the ruler who won the Battle of Nuʻuanu to become the first king of a unified Hawaii.
question.answerHtml: Kamehameha [accept Kamehameha II; accept Kamehameha I or Kamehameha the Great]
question.clue: The third person of this name was inspired by William Richards to issue the Edict of Toleration and Declaration of Rights, which introduced a legislature and supreme court to his country.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about interactions between early European explorers and the Maori: (MAO-ree).
swap.text: This British explorer made contact with the Maori in 1769. This explorer reached locations including Hawai'i and Australia, and lends their name to the strait separating the islands of New Zealand.
swap.clue: On this man's first voyage, which was to observe the Transit of Venus, no one died of scurvy because of his insistence of eating fruits and sauerkraut.

question.leadin: James Prendergast called this document a "simple nullity" in an 1877 court case.
question.text: Name this 1840 treaty between the British Empire and over 500 Maori chiefs. Translators questionably used the words "kawanatanga" and "rangatiratanga" to refer to "government" and "chieftainship" in this treaty.
question.clue: The Native Land Act of 1862 struck down the land-selling article, which had been the cause of the Wairau incident led by Te Rauparaha.

swap.leadin: The women's Mau movement emerged to oppose colonial rule in this country after the Black Saturday massacre.
swap.text: Name this Polynesian country where the Mau movement opposed New Zealand's colonial rule in the late 1920s and early 1930s. This country was colonized after German-backed rebels were defeated in the Siege of Apia.
swap.answerHtml: Independent State of Samoa [accept Western Samoa; do NOT accept or prompt on “American Samoa”]

question.leadin: Robert Louis Stevenson's book A Footnote to History describes how a diplomatic standoff in this country was averted when a cyclone wrecked all the warships in its harbor.
question.text: Name this modern-day country whose independence was advocated for by the Mau movement. Germany was granted administration of this island country in 1899, while the US administered a set of islands to the east.
question.clue: This country's independence was demanded on "Black Saturday" by the Olaf Frderick Nelson-led Mau Movement.

swap.text: This location became a popular metonym for Australian penal colonies despite being ruled unsuitable for settlement upon the landing of the First Fleet. The planned penal colony for this location was later relocated north to Port Jackson.
swap.clue: Fed by the Georges and Cooks Rivers, its north shore is home to Kingsford Smith airport.

question.leadin: One of these structures known as "A Kivi" was significantly less disturbed than others due to being located inland, with statues on it unusually facing the ocean.
question.text: Name these large ceremonial stone platforms atop which moai statues were placed.

swap.leadin: Lorrin Thurston and John L. Stephens led the overthrow this monarch, establishing a government under Sanford Dole.
swap.text: Name this monarch who resisted the influence of the Missionary Party in the wake of the Bayonet Constitution being forced on her brother David.
swap.clue: A group of revolutionaries known as a "committee of public safety" and led by Lorrin Thurston rebelled against this leader in order to gain rights for citizens born of American parents.

question.text: The US Navy's victory at the Battle of the Coral Sea foiled this Japanese operation, whose goal was to capture Port Moresby in New Guinea and set the stage for an invasion of Australia.

swap.text: This favorite wife of Kamehameha, on the other hand, converted to Protestantism and embarked on a campaign of destroying sacred Hawaiian sites and promoting literacy so that Hawaiians could read the Bible.

question.leadin: Native speakers of this language started to use the word palapala in the 1820s to refer to the body of written knowledge produced with the help of Christian missionaries.
question.text: Name this language. The nineteenth-century historians Davida Malo and "Kepelino" both wrote in this language, and Lorrin A. Thurston wrote a constitution in this language.

swap.leadin: According to legend, Halley's Comet was in the sky when this ruler was born, leading to a prophecy that he would be a great killer of chiefs.
swap.text: Name this native ruler who unified the Hawaiian Islands.
swap.clue: After being attacked by fishermen during a war, this king promoted the safety of civilians in the Law of the Splintered Paddle.
